title: Minimal path from supervised flow to limited automation
summary: Shortest safe path is to add an automated read-only runner first, then promote the same loop to auto-enqueue, and only later allow token/config-gated auto-submit for one symbol, one contract, LIMIT only.

current_starting_point.starts_from: Existing supervised batch planning flow that produces READY/BLOCKED candidates without writing when run with --no-write.
automation_ready_parts: queue/executor path already used by supervised live flow

minimal_automation_path: Step 1: read_only loop runs supervised_batch_plan for one symbol on a timer and records readiness/guards only.
Step 2: auto_enqueue only writes READY candidates into action_queue, still no exchange submit.
Step 3: auto_submit allows one symbol, one contract, LIMIT only, after queue/reconcile guards pass.

exact_modules_needed.role: CLI entry for repeated read-only planning.
Batch candidate assembly and READY/BLOCKED output.
Single-symbol strategy proposal and safety evaluation.
Minimal auto_enqueue target once read-only loop is proven.
Existing queue-to-direct-API executor for later auto_submit mode.

required_flags_modes: read_only: no DB writes except optional external status log, no queue writes, no exchange action.
auto_enqueue: enqueue READY candidates only, no executor submit.
auto_submit: execute queued LIMIT action for allowlisted symbol only.
hard_safety_rules: Allowlist exactly one symbol at first.
Respect gross cap before enqueue and before submit.
Block new OPEN when profitable-lot guard blocks.
Require lot-entry spacing guard to pass.
Require no active queue/pending LIMIT/pending CHASE conflict.
Reconcile after every submitted action before any next submit.

no_code_conclusion.reason: It proves timing, logging, readiness transitions, and guard stability without queue writes or exchange risk.
